questions.text: What is the maximum number of complete circles that will be seen, if the strips given below are re-arranged without rotating?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Number the strips 1 to 6 from the left. Match each part-circle on a strip's right edge with one of the same height and size on another strip's left edge. The matches chain all six strips into one order: 2, 6, 4, 1, 5, 3. In that order the cut arcs join into six circles (strips 2-6, 2-6-4, 6-4, 4-1-5, 1-5-3 and 5-3), and strip 5 already holds one small complete circle, so 7 complete circles are seen.

questions.text: What is the total number of triangles in the figure given below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Label every point where lines meet and list each straight line with the points on it. A triangle needs three points joined pairwise by three different straight lines. Going through the points one at a time, and counting each triangle only from its first point, gives 24 triangles.

questions.text: Given below are ten pieces of a puzzle. When arranged correctly they form a four-digit number. What is the number formed after the correct arrangement?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Five pieces show the tops of digits (a top edge or top bar visible) and five show the bottoms (a bottom curve visible). The top pieces chain as: a round bowl, the top bar and stem of a 5, the hooked top of a 6, and the top of a 3. The bottom pieces chain as: a closed lower bowl, the bowl of the 5, the closed bowl of the 6, and the lower bowl of the 3. The first digit has a closed bowl on top and another closed bowl below, so it is 8, and the number is 8563.

questions.text: A perspective view of a solid is shown below. The solid is symmetrical, and hidden surfaces such as the base are flat. What is the total number of surfaces in the solid?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Read the solid as a tall central block with four stepped arms, each arm made of a raised plateau, an end tab, a small sunken pocket and a groove next to the central block. Count the flat horizontal top faces: 1 for the central block and 4 in each arm, giving 17. Count the vertical faces you can see, merging walls that lie in one plane: 27. The solid looks the same after a half turn, so every hidden wall matches a visible one, giving 27 more. With the flat base, the total is 17 + 27 + 27 + 1 = 72.

questions.text: A perspective view of a solid object is shown on the left. The object is cut simultaneously along THREE perpendicular planes as shown on the right. How many surfaces will the resulting pieces have in total (i.e. sum of the surfaces of all pieces)?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The side view shows a horizontal cut through the cone above its base, and the top view shows two vertical cuts through the axis. The cone tip is split into 4 pieces, each with a curved surface, two flat cut faces and a flat bottom: 4 surfaces each, 16 in all. The lower part is 4 pieces, each with the flat top of the cut cone, the curved cone surface, the top of the slab, two outer slab sides, the slab bottom and two cut faces: 8 surfaces each, 32 in all. Total 16 + 32 = 48.

questions.text: A typical football is made by stitching together 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons. How many vertices (junctions) are there in such a football?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The patches have 12 x 5 + 20 x 6 = 180 corners in total. Each junction on the ball is shared by 3 patches, so the number of vertices is 180 / 3 = 60.

questions.text: A vehicle with a wheel arrangement is shown in Figure (i). This vehicle is travelling along a circular path as shown in Figure (ii). The wheels do not change their orientation while moving along the circular path. Figure (iii) shows the location of the centres of the wheels. The distance between the centres of Wheel-3 and Wheel-2 is 170 cm, and the distance between the centres of Wheel-1 and Wheel-2 is 180 cm. The radius of the circular path followed by Wheel-2 is 525 cm. What is the radius of the path followed by Wheel-1 in cm?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Wheels 2 and 3 share an axle that points at the centre of the circle, with Wheel-2 on the inside. The midpoint of Wheels 2 and 3 is 85 cm further out, at radius 525 + 85 = 610 cm. Wheel-1 lies ahead of that midpoint along the direction of travel, by \(\sqrt{180^2 - 85^2} = \sqrt{25175} \approx 158.7\) cm. So its radius is \(\sqrt{610^2 + 25175} = \sqrt{397275} \approx 630.3\) cm.

questions.text: Shown below is an image of a circle and six equilateral triangles. The circumference of the circle is 18.85 cm. What is the area of ONE equilateral triangle in cm2? Assume √3 = 1.732 and π = 3.14.
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Radius = 18.85 / (2 x 3.14) = 3 cm. The circle touches the inner base of each triangle and the six triangles surround a regular hexagon whose side equals the triangle side, so the circle is the hexagon's incircle: side = 2r / \(\sqrt{3}\) = 6 / 1.732 = 3.464 cm. Area of one triangle = (1.732 / 4) x 3.464 x 3.464 = 0.433 x 12 = 5.196, about 5.2 cm2.

questions.text: A wooden block of dimension 10cm x 20cm x 30cm is cut into equal sized planks. The cut planks are stacked one above the other to achieve a total height of 100cm exactly. If the minimum number of planks are cut to achieve this height, then what is the volume of each plank in cm3?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning

questions.text: Shown below are two stacked paper cups and a box with their dimensions. If stacking is allowed, then what is the maximum number of cups that can be stored in the box without deforming the cups?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: A stack of k cups is 4 + 0.5(k - 1) cm long and 4 cm wide. Standing upright in the 6 cm deep box, a stack holds 5 cups and 4 x 3 = 12 stacks fit, so 60 cups. Laid on their side along the 16 cm length, a stack holds 25 cups (4 + 24 x 0.5 = 16), three stacks fit across the 12 cm width and one layer fits in the 6 cm height: 3 x 25 = 75 cups, the maximum.

The centres of the spheres coincide with the corners of the tetrahedron. What is the radius (in cm) of the largest sphere that can be accommodated within the tetrahedron?

questions.text: Section P shows three views of a regular dice. TEN of such regular dice are stacked on an opaque table as shown in Section Q (two views of the same arrangement). What is the maximum sum that can be achieved adding the numbers on the visible surfaces from all angles?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Section P shows opposite faces add to 7 (6-1, 5-2, 4-3). The stack is a corner staircase: 6 dice on the table, 3 on the second level, 1 on top. Best totals by how many faces show: 1 face gives 6, 2 adjacent faces 11, 3 faces at a corner 15, 4 faces (hiding 1 and 2, which are adjacent) 18, 5 faces (hiding 1) 20. Bottom layer: 11 + 6 + 6 + 15 + 18 + 18 = 74. Middle layer: 11 + 18 + 18 = 47. Top die: 20. Total 74 + 47 + 20 = 141.

questions.text: Alphabets A to Z are arranged starting at 6’o clock, and three alphabets with their respective positions are shown in the image given below. Which of the following combinations is/are correct?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: A is at 6 o'clock, J at 7:30 and K at 9, so letters move clockwise in steps of 1.5 hours and the 8 marked positions repeat every 8 letters (N, the 14th letter, lands at 1:30, which checks). A letter's position depends on its place in the alphabet minus 1, divided by 8: remainder 0 is 6 o'clock, 2 is 9 o'clock, 6 is 3 o'clock. G and O give 3 o'clock and A gives 6, so A is right. S and K give 9 o'clock and Y gives 6, so B is right. F is at 1:30 and B is at 7:30, so C and D are wrong.

questions.text: Which option(s) contain(s) the exact fragments of the image shown on the left?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.subtopic: Matching a part to the whole
questions.solution: Lay each option square over the image at the same size and check every fragment in place. In B the cross, the corner at the top right, the bend where the horizontal line meets the slanted line and the vertical line with the wave above it all sit exactly where they are in the image. D's cross, plus sign, corner, small bend and wave also match. A has a straight line that would continue the long top-left diagonal past the point where it ends, and C has a line that turns along the circle about 10 units below where the circle really is, so A and C are not exact.

questions.text: Which of the options is/are correct according to pigment colour theory?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: In pigment (subtractive) theory the primaries are red, yellow and blue, and the wheel runs yellow, orange, red, violet, blue, green in order. A shows the three primaries pointing at their own colours on a complete 12-part wheel. D shows the three secondaries (green, orange, violet) each pointing at its place on a correct wheel. B's wheel has yellow where orange should be, and C's triangle (violet, yellow, green) is not a primary or secondary set and its wheel has no orange.

questions.text: Four spheres start revolving clockwise in concentric circles from their initial positions as shown below. Yellow travels at 2m/sec, green at 4m/sec, red at 2m/sec and blue at 4m/sec. Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?

options.label: A
options.text: Yellow and green never cross (overtake) each other

options.label: B
options.text: Red and blue takes the same time to complete one revolution

options.label: C
options.text: Yellow takes less time than green to complete one revolution

options.label: D
options.text: Blue and red will cross each other twice after the first 3 complete revolutions of blue

questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Yellow is on the 3 m circle, green on 6 m, red on 8 m and blue on 12 m. Times for one revolution: yellow \(2\pi \times 3/2 = 3\pi\) s, green \(2\pi \times 6/4 = 3\pi\) s, red \(2\pi \times 8/2 = 8\pi\) s, blue \(2\pi \times 12/4 = 6\pi\) s. Yellow and green turn at the same rate and stay half a turn apart, so A is true and C is false. Red and blue take different times, so B is false. In blue's first 3 revolutions (\(18\pi\) s) blue gains only three quarters of a turn on red, so they cross only once, and D is false.

questions.text: Shown below is a cross-section of two different trees of same species and age but found in different locations. Based on the image, which of the statement(s) is/are TRUE.

options.label: A
options.text: Growth of the tree X is more consistent than tree Y

options.label: B
options.text: Growth of the tree X is healthier than tree Y

options.label: C
options.text: Climatic conditions could be the reason for the uneven ring structures in tree Y

options.label: D
options.text: Growth of the tree Y is healthier than tree X

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Each ring is one year of growth and its width shows how much the tree grew that year. X has evenly spaced, wide rings, so it grew steadily and well (A and B). Y has a band of very tightly packed rings, years of poor growth, which is typically caused by drought or other harsh climate (C). So D is false.

questions.text: Six concentric white rings, each of equal thickness but having different diameters, are positioned on different planes in space. A one-point perspective view of the rings is shown below. Based on this view, which of the option(s) is/are TRUE?

options.label: A
options.text: Rings 6 and 3 are closer to the viewer compared to ring 5

options.label: B
options.text: Rings 2 and 4 are at equal distance from the viewer

options.label: C
options.text: Ring 1 is the nearest to the viewer

options.label: D
options.text: Ring 5 is the farthest from the viewer

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: All rings are equally thick, so in perspective a ring looks thicker the closer it is. Measured thicknesses: ring 1 about 44 units, rings 3 and 6 about 21, ring 5 about 12, rings 2 and 4 about 6. So ring 1 is nearest (C), rings 3 and 6 are nearer than ring 5 (A), and rings 2 and 4 are equally far (B). Rings 2 and 4 are farther than ring 5, so D is false.

questions.text: Which of the options can be created by the stamp shown on the left?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: A stamp prints the mirror image of its face, and it can be pressed at any angle, so every rotation of that mirror image is possible. A, B and D are the same design turned by 90 or 180 degrees (D turned 180 degrees gives A, and turned 90 degrees gives B). C differs only in the centre E, which makes it the mirror image of the others, and it matches the stamp face as seen, not its print. So A, B and D can be made.

questions.text: Tile X was used to create a pattern which is seamless (without gaps) when arranged as shown in Y. Which tile(s) from the options will create a seamless pattern?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: In Y the tiles are repeated by sliding one tile-width across and one tile-height down, so every bump on one edge must fit a matching dent on the opposite edge. B's top zigzag is exactly its bottom zigzag, and its left and right edges are straight. C's left dent matches its right bump, its top steps match its bottom steps, and its top-left slope matches its bottom-right slope one step across and down. A's sloped top does not match its flat bottom, and D has bumps on both left and right, so neither fits.

questions.text: If the image on the left is flipped horizontally (about Y-axis), and then rotated 180 degrees, what will be the resulting image?

questions.text: Which option represents the data in the pie-chart?

So the bars must fall in that order with orange just taller than white and green clearly shorter than white. questions.text: Shutter speed is one of the parameters by which exposure of the image can be controlled. How does shutter speed control exposure?

options.label: A
options.text: By increasing the size of the opening through which light enters the camera.

options.label: B
options.text: By increasing sensitivity of the image sensor.

options.label: C
options.text: By increasing the time for light to enter the camera.

options.label: D
options.text: By increasing the number of pixels in the image.

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Shutter speed is how long the shutter stays open, so it controls the time for which light reaches the sensor. The size of the opening is the aperture (A), sensor sensitivity is ISO (B), and the pixel count is resolution (D), none of which is shutter speed.

questions.text: A cube, a triangular prism and a square pyramid of equal height are resting on a surface along a straight line, arranged in a random order. If the source of light is fixed and the light rays are parallel, which of the option shows the shadows correctly in top view?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: With equal heights and parallel rays, the top of each solid throws its shadow the same distance in the same direction. The pyramid's apex shadow must sit as far from the base centre as the cube's top corners are from their bases, and the prism's ridge shadow the same. In A and C the prism or pyramid shadow reaches too far, in B the pyramid shadow is too long; only D keeps all three offsets equal.

questions.text: A ball with a thin elastic rod moves from left to right as shown below. Which option represents the movement of the rod?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: The balls are close together at the start (speeding up), far apart in the middle (fast) and close again at the end (slowing down). While the ball speeds up and moves fast, the rod's tip lags behind, bending back to the left more and more. When the ball slows and stops, the tip swings forward past upright and wobbles. Option A shows this; B bends the wrong way, C stays stiff while the ball speeds up, and D snaps upright in the middle.

questions.text: A cyclist was peddling a geared cycle on an upward inclined road and decided to stop on the incline. Which option can be used to stop the bicycle on the incline only using force on foot pedals?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: To hold the bicycle still using only pedal force, the gear must give the most turning force at the wheel for a given push: the smallest front chainring with the largest rear sprocket. Option B has exactly this lowest gear. A uses the largest chainring with the smallest sprocket (the hardest gear), and C and D use the large chainring.

questions.text: During a long-distance sea voyage, without the Captain realising, steering of the ship started malfunctioning in the following manner. When the Captain was trying to turn the ship 60 degrees to the left, ship was turning 30 degrees to the right. When the Captain was trying to turn the ship 90 degrees to the left, ship was turning 90 degrees to the right. When the Captain was trying to turn the ship 45 degrees to the right, ship was turning 30 degrees to the left. When the Captain was trying to turn the ship 90 degrees to the right, ship was turning 45 degrees to the left. Before the malfunction, ship was going in North-East direction. After the malfunction started, without realising the problem, the Captain tried to turn 90 degrees to the left, then 90 degrees to the right, then 45 degrees to the right and finally 60 degrees to the left. Find the current direction of the ship.
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Replace each command with what the ship actually does. Left 90 makes it turn right 90: North-East becomes South-East. Right 90 makes it turn left 45: South-East becomes East. Right 45 makes it turn left 30: East becomes 30 degrees north of East. Left 60 makes it turn right 30: back to East.

questions.text: A hollow paper cone is cut by a spiral blade. The blade, the cone, the position of the cone and blade, and the line along which it gets cut are shown below. The surface of the cone is then unwrapped on a flat surface. Which option shows the unwrapped surface?

Each place where a rim meets the cut is a corner, so the outline must have exactly four corners: the two tips plus one corner on each side. A has these; B and D are smooth on one side, and C has an extra kink.
